title: [Kernel] LoRA triton kernels support PDL (#27402)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-11-19 > 2025-11-07); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.

workload.note: lora_shrink + lora_expand back to back (a LoRA linear) via LoRAKernelMeta: hidden 4096, rank 16, 1 LoRA, 1 and 3 slices, 16 and 256 tokens; PR = PDL (griddepcontrol) in the LoRA Triton kernels (sm_90+, sm_120 ok). CUDA-event us per shrink+expand pair. Author: '5-20% kernel runtime speedup' + Qwen3-30B-A3B LoRA serving on H20 (reported-only).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

policy.machine_snapshot: machine.py snapshot per workload run -> data/pr_<n>/work/machine_<arm>_<i>.json

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY task.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

metrics.name: serving_output_throughput
metrics.parse: Output token throughput (not measured: Qwen3-30B-A3B + LoRA, H20)

headline: lora_shrink_expand_1slice_t16

reported.gain_evidence: This is a good feature to have, see following results, we generally see 5% to 20% kernel runtime speedup for smaller Ms.
reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

author_hardware_args.text: vllm bench serve --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --metric-percentiles 90 --model test_lora_model --num-prompts 100 --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 1024 --request-rate inf

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_27402:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:27402 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_27402:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:27402 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 /task/bench.py'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).

test_note: perf-only PDL flags on LoRA Triton kernels; no test in the diff; needs sm_90+ (sm_120 ok).
